newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Woodside looks to start Laminaria.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Woodside looks to start Laminaria.

text.p: Woodside Petroleum Ltd said on Friday it expects to receive a production licence from the Federal and Northern Territory governments this month to enable it to develop the Laminaria and Corallina oil fields.
Woodside has said development of the offshore fields would cost an estimated A$900 million.
Woodside holds a 50 percent interest in the Timor Sea permit AC/P8 while Broken Hill Pty Co Ltd and Royal Dutch/Shell each hold 25 percent,
A proposed production platform would have a maximum capacity to produce 170,000 barrels of light crude per day, a Woodside spokesman said.
A contract for construction of the whole of the platform has already been let to Samsung Heavy Industries Co Ltd of South Korea, he said.
"We wanted to book time as soon as we could in their yard in Korea," he said.
The project is expected to commence production in early 1999, he said.

Woodside also expects to boost production of condensate at its Goodwyn platform in the North West Shelf to about 100,000 barrels per day from the current 70,000 barrels by expanding its condensate stabilising facilities onshore.
Equal one-sixth partners in the North West Shelf are Chevron, BHP, Shell, British Petroleum Co Plc, Japan Australia LNG (MiMi) and operator Woodside.
This would relieve a bottleneck problem that currently exists, the spokesman said.
